subtype: Approach: teaching the plan to grandparents [Action]
passage: At the community centre's senior club, Baljeet unrolled a sheet of chart paper and taped it to the board. Three lines in big Hindi letters. Line one: OTP किसी को नहीं बताना, never share the OTP. Line two: फ़ोन काटो, परिवार को फ़ोन करो, put the phone down and ring the family. Line three: इनाम के लिए पैसे नहीं देना, no money for prizes. Baljeet read each line aloud and asked the group to repeat it. Baljeet's grandfather Kunal squinted, then nodded. “Short enough that I'll remember.” His wife, Baljeet's grandmother, asked for a copy. That evening Baljeet taped a smaller sheet next to the landline at home, at the height of Dada's eyes.

qa.q: What are the three rules on the chart?
qa.a: Never share the OTP, put the phone down and ring the family, and no money for prizes.

qa.q: What might Baljeet be feeling as the group repeats the lines?
qa.a: Proud and a little anxious: Baljeet hopes the grandparents will really remember them when the phone rings.

qa.q: What else could Baljeet do to help them remember, and why?
qa.a: Practise a pretend call with them at home, since saying the lines aloud once makes them easier to use under pressure.

qa.q: How does the list look to Baljeet's grandfather?
qa.a: Kunal finds it short and clear, in a language he reads easily, so it is something he can hold onto when a caller sounds convincing.

grounding: A teen writes a short Hindi list for grandparents and posts it near the landline.

subtype: Approach: teaching the plan to grandparents [Action]
passage:
Dear Dadi and Dada,
I'm leaving this letter with the card I've stuck next to your landline, so you know why it's there.
Last month your neighbour lost money to a caller who said he was from the bank. It scared me. So Divyansh and I wrote three rules in Hindi, in big letters:
1. OTP kabhi kisi ko mat batana. (Never tell anyone an OTP.)
2. Shak ho to phone rakho, aur ghar par phone karo. (If in doubt, hang up and ring someone in the family.)
3. Inaam ke liye paisa kabhi mat do. (Never pay money for a prize.)
Below the rules, Divyansh wrote Papa's number and mine.
When I come on Sunday, let's practise once. I'll pretend to be a caller, and you say rule 2 and hang up on me. You're allowed to enjoy that part.
With love,
Francis

qa.q: Whose numbers did Divyansh write below the rules?
How did the neighbour's loss make Francis feel?
qa.a: It scared Francis, and that worry turned into a practical plan to protect Dadi and Dada.

qa.q: Why would a practice call on Sunday help beyond the written card?
qa.a: Saying rule 2 aloud and hanging up once makes it easier to do under real pressure, not just to read it.

qa.q: How might Dadi and Dada feel finding the card and the letter?
qa.a: They may feel cared for and a little amused, and more confident knowing exactly what to do when a strange call comes.

grounding: Shows a teen writing a short Hindi list for grandparents: never share an OTP, hang up and call family, never pay for prizes, placed by their landline.

subtype: Approach: teaching the plan to grandparents [Action]
passage:
So Vijay, you asked what I did in the holidays. Mostly this. I'm Omkar, and I became my grandparents' anti-scam teacher.
Nanaji had got two calls in one week: one “bank officer”, one “you've won a prize”. He didn't fall for them, but he told me he nearly pressed a button on the second. That scared me.
So I sat at their dining table with a sheet of chart paper and wrote in big Hindi letters: never share OTP; if unsure, hang up and call family; no payment for any prize. Nani made me add Mummy's number in red. We stuck it on the wall right above their landline, at eye level.
Then we practised. I'd ring the landline from my phone and play a fake officer, and Nani would read line two and hang up on me. She got very good at hanging up on me.
Last week a real one called. Nanaji just pointed at the chart and put the phone down.

qa.q: Where did they stick the chart paper?
qa.a: On the wall right above their landline, at eye level.

qa.q: How did Omkar feel on hearing that Nanaji nearly pressed a button?
qa.a: Omkar felt scared for Nanaji, and that worry pushed a practical plan into action.

qa.q: What made the plan work beyond the chart itself?
qa.a: The practice calls, because Nani rehearsed reading line two and hanging up until it felt natural.

qa.q: How did the plan look to Nanaji when the real call came?
qa.a: Nanaji felt sure enough to just point at the chart and put the phone down, with nothing left to decide.

grounding: Shows a teen writing a short Hindi list for grandparents with never share OTP, hang up and call family, and no payment for prizes, stuck near their landline.
